results_section.claim: 3. The structured traces reveal distinct accuracy patterns across our four reasoning priorities: Comparison Analysis (39.6%), Numerical Verification (36.3%), Superlative Reasoning (30.4%), and Entity Heuristic (26.7%).
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: The file outputs/error_analysis.json contains priority_performance field showing: COMPARISON_ANALYSIS='65/164 (39.6%)', NUMERICAL_VERIFICATION='223/614 (36.3%)', ENTITY_HEURISTIC='92/344 (26.7%)', SUPERLATIVE_REASONING='31/102 (30.4%)'. All four values match exactly.

results_section.claim: 4. unit-aware claims achieve 38.1% accuracy compared to 33.6% overall
results_section.explanation: Analysis stage: The file outputs/error_analysis.json contains unit_aware_accuracy=0.38064516129032255 (~38.1%) and overall_accuracy=0.33578431372549017 (~33.6%), exactly matching both claimed values.

results_section.claim: 2. Analysis of failure cases reveals that UnitMath successfully prevents 78% of unit-related errors that occur in baseline systems: scale confusions (1000 vs. 1,000,000), unit mismatches (comparing mass to volume), and percentage-type errors.

However, the error_analysis.json error_distribution only shows 'other': 813 — unit-specific error categorization produced no output. The 78% metric does not appear in any output file. Static inspection cannot establish a reliable provenance chain for this claim.

results_section.claim: 5. Claims involving unit conversions (mg ↔ g, percentage ↔ decimal) achieve 85% accuracy, while dimensionally invalid comparisons (mass vs. volume) are correctly refused with explicit error reporting.
